To say what you want to do: verb + たい です.
To say what you want to have: X が ほしい です.
To say the purpose of going somewhere: X に いきます (かいもの に, およぎ に).
To use なにか / どこか (something / somewhere).
To make a wish list for the trip to Japan.
The wish list
In two months, Mihai and Ana are leaving for Japan. At Kenji’s café, each of them writes their wish list.
Mihai, what do you want to do in Japan?
First I want to see Fuji. Then I want to get into a hot spring.
I want to wear a kimono in Kyoto. And I want to drink matcha.
Do you want to climb Fuji?
No, I don’t want to climb it. Because it’s cold in autumn. Just see it.
And what will you do in Tokyo?
I want to go shopping in Akihabara! Because I want a new camera.
I want to go to a bookshop to buy Japanese books.
And the food? What do you want to eat?
Sushi, tempura and… real ramen!
Real? My ramen isn’t real?!
Ah… no, Kenji’s ramen is the best! I meant I want to eat it in Japan too.
Hahaha. Then eat my wife’s okonomiyaki in Hiroshima.
Definitely! Kenji, do you want anything? We’ll buy you a souvenir.
I don’t need anything. But… I could eat a little momiji-manjū from Hiroshima.

(isn’t it)
“-tai” is pronounced like English “tie”. たべたい = ta-be-tie, not “tabetaii”.
The i in し is swallowed: “hoshii” sounds almost like “hosh’ii”. The last i is long.
ん before や is nasal and doesn’t merge: hon-ya, not “ho-nya”. In romaji it’s written with an apostrophe: hon'ya.
1. I want to do: ～たい です
Take the ～ます form, drop ます and add たい です. たい behaves like an -い adjective.
ます form
Being an -い adjective, it has the same forms as in chapter 7: negative ～たく ありません (or ～たくない です), past ～たかった です.
I don’t want to do anything today.
When I was a child, I wanted to be a pilot.
The object can be marked with が or を: すし が たべたい / すし を たべたい. Both are correct. が is slightly more natural.
2. I want to have: X が ほしい です
For THINGS (not actions) use ほしい, also an -い adjective, with が:
I want a car.
What do you want (me to get you)?
Don’t confuse: “I want a coffee” = コーヒー が ほしい です (the thing), but “I want to drink a coffee” = コーヒー が のみたい です (the action).
3. Politeness: don’t ask a superior what they “want”
In Japanese, “～たい です か” and “ほしい です か” sound too direct to a teacher, a boss or a customer. With them, offer something with ～ませんか or いかが です か: コーヒー は いかが です か (Would you like a coffee?).
And you don’t say directly what others want (you can’t know what they feel): for the third person you use ～たがって います, which you’ll learn at N4.
Between friends, なに が たべたい? (without です か) is perfectly normal.
4. Purpose: X に いきます
To say WHY you’re going somewhere: PURPOSE に + いきます / きます / かえります. The purpose can be:
An action noun
I go shopping
I go out to eat
A verb (the ます form without ます)
I go swimming
I go to buy a book
I’m going to the airport to pick up my friend.
The full order: PLACE へ — PURPOSE に — いきます. デパート へ くつ を かい に いきます.

ゆめ の リスト — Yuki’s dream list
At the Friday club, everyone wrote down their dreams. Yuki read hers out loud.
I have lots of dreams.
First, I want to speak Spanish better. I want to read Spanish newspapers without a dictionary.
Next, I want to travel to different cities in Spain. I want to see flamenco in Seville.
Then, I want a little house. I want to plant a cherry tree in the garden.
I want a dog too. But because Tama wouldn’t put up with it, a cat would be better.
The last dream is a secret. I don’t want to tell anyone!
Everyone laughed. But only Ana looked at Mihai and smiled.

タマ の ゆめ — Tama’s dream
I’m Tama. I’m the cat who lives in the university library.
I’m seven years old. For a cat, I’m a grown-up.
Humans are always talking about “what do I want to do?” and “what do I want to have?”.
Today I want to tell you about my dreams.
First, I want to sleep in a warm place every day.
In front of the library window, it gets very warm in the afternoon.
But there’s always a student sitting there. It’s my spot, you know!
Next, I want to eat fish. Every day.
But Mrs Suzuki says: “Tama is on a diet.”
I don’t want to be on a diet. I don’t want to at all!
Kenji sometimes gives me fish in secret. I love Kenji.
Then, I want to see my children.
I had three kittens. Now they all live in different homes.
The white one is in Mrs Suzuki’s flat. Next to Mihai.
The black one is at Carlos’s. The tabby is at Hanako’s.
They’re all well. But sometimes I miss them. Because I’m their mother.
Finally, I have one biggest dream.
I want to go to Japan.
Mrs Suzuki often talks about Japan.
They say there are cat islands in Japan. Islands with more cats than people!
They say cats are the most important there. Wonderful, isn’t it?
The other day, Mihai and Ana were talking about the trip to Japan.
I climbed into Mihai’s bag.
“Tama! What are you doing?” Mihai jumped.
“Does Tama want to go to Japan too?” Ana laughed.
“Miaow!” Yes, I want to go. Definitely!
But Mihai took me out of the bag.
“Sorry, Tama. Cats can’t get on planes.”
Liar! Mrs Suzuki said “animals can get on too”!
But I’m a bit scared of planes. And fourteen hours is a long time.
So, instead, I asked for a favour.
I pressed my head against Mihai’s leg and said “miaow”.
Mihai understood. “You want a souvenir. I’ll bring you photos from the cat island.”
For a human, Mihai is quite clever.
Now I’m sleeping in front of the window. There’s no student today. …It’s a good day.
